task_description: You find personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information in a document. Return a JSON object {"entities": [{"text": ..., "type": ...}]} listing every PII span in the order it appears. "text" is copied exactly from the document. "type" is one of: account_number, address, api_key, bank_routing_number, biometric_identifier, certificate_license_number, city, company_name, coordinate, country, credit_card_number, customer_id, cvv, date, date_of_birth, date_time, device_identifier, email, employee_id, first_name, health_plan_beneficiary_number, ipv4, ipv6, last_name, license_plate, medical_record_number, name, national_id, password, phone_number, pin, postcode, ssn, state, street_address, swift_bic, tax_id, time, unique_identifier, url, user_name, vehicle_identifier. Use the most specific type (first_name/last_name for a split name, name for a full name). Do not list non-personal values such as product codes, prices or generic dates that do not identify a person. If there is no PII, return {"entities": []}. Output JSON only. Labelling conventions: a plain two-part name (Lisa Robertson) is split into first_name and last_name; a name with a title, middle name or middle initial (Dr. Warren Thompson, Debra B. Maldonado) is one name; an address written as one run with its city, postcode or country is one street_address; use the specific identifier type (medical_record_number, customer_id, employee_id, license_plate, vehicle_identifier) and unique_identifier only when none fits; a date of birth is date_of_birth, a date with a clock time is date_time. Values written as a list ('C80-1981-209, ID-513-I') are separate spans. Label every code that identifies a person or record by its prefix or field label, whatever the document is about (MED2791810 is a medical_record_number even in an IT incident report).
llm_as_a_judge_instructions: Compare the predicted entities with the reference entities. Count a reference entity as found when the prediction contains the same text (ignoring case and surrounding whitespace) with the same or an equivalent type. Output the F1 score between predicted and reference entities as a number between 0 and 1 inside the score tag, for example <score>0.8</score>. Output 1 when both lists are empty.
synthetic_data_generation_instructions: Each input is a short passage from a business, legal, medical, financial, HR, logistics or technical document, with realistic fake personal data embedded. Most inputs hold 2-7 PII spans; about one input in forty holds none, only non-personal values such as prices, quantities, product codes or section numbers. Mix the types widely across the task description's list, and use varied realistic formats: record numbers such as MRN-656301, MED38325654, EMP806261, CUST9988564, A4050927; national ids such as ZZ 670882 T or 065 273 856; dates such as 1989-10-10, 04/27/1989, 09.09.1981, Sep 09, 2011 and 1975-06-22T21:42:20; IPv4 and IPv6 addresses; coordinates such as -17.490129,7.321645; phone numbers and street addresses from the US, UK, India and Australia. The answer lists every PII span in the order it appears, with text copied character for character from the input. Labelling conventions: (1) Names: a plain two-part name written together (Lisa Robertson, Betty Hill-Brady) is split into a first_name entity and a last_name entity; a name with a title, a middle name or a middle initial (Dr. Warren Thompson, Debra B. Maldonado, Scott Christopher Burgess) is one name entity; a lone given name or surname is first_name or last_name. (2) Addresses: an address written as one run, with its city, postcode, state or country (H.No. 99 Seth Path, 289030, Bulandshahr; 483 Eric Plains, Thomasmouth, Mozambique) is one street_address entity, not split; use city, state, postcode and country only when they stand in their own field or sentence. (3) Identifiers: use the specific type whenever the context or prefix shows it (medical record numbers such as MRN-/MED- numbers are medical_record_number, customer and client numbers are customer_id, staff numbers are employee_id, plate numbers are license_plate, a 17-character VIN is vehicle_identifier); unique_identifier only when no specific type fits. (4) Dates: a date of birth is date_of_birth, a date with a clock time is date_time, other dates tied to a person or record are date.
